r1.content: Many modern trail and enduro bikes run a 29" front wheel and a 27.5" rear wheel. Front and rear tires and tubes are then different sizes. Always confirm which wheel a tire or tube is for. Some bikes are mullets only in smaller frame sizes, so check the frame size too.
r1.heading: Mixed wheels ("mullet") bikes

r1.content: Pick the bike from the catalog whenever you can: make, model and year. The same model name can have completely different parts in different years; a 2012 Fuel EX 8 and a 2023 Fuel EX 8 Gen 6 share almost nothing. If the customer doesn't know the year, ask for a photo or check the serial and frame stickers before quoting parts. For derailleur hangers, match by photo, not model year, because frames change mid-year.
r1.heading: Identify the bike first

r1.content: For a flat, find the cause before fitting a new tube, or it'll flat again. Common causes: a thorn or glass still in the tire, a pinch flat from low pressure (two small slits side by side), a rim tape that's shifted and exposed a spoke hole, or a worn-out tire. A fix with a new tube is `FLAT-REPAIR`, and it needs a tube on the order: a sized tube when the tire size is known, otherwise the generic tube, which the mechanic sizes at the bench. Repeated flats from the same spot point to the rim tape or something stuck in the tire. A cut sidewall needs a new tire (`TIRE-INSTALL`). A new tire on a tubed wheel needs a tube too; a tubeless wheel needs `TUBELESS-SETUP` instead. High-end bikes usually run tubeless and entry-level bikes run tubes, but ask the customer when it matters for the order.
r1.heading: Flat tires

- Brakes that don't stop the bike reliably: a lever to the bar that no longer stops the bike, contaminated pads or rotors, leaking hydraulics, pads worn through or down to the wear line.

r1.content: A knock or clunk from the front of the bike is often blamed on the fork, but a loose headset feels and sounds almost the same. Check headset play first by holding the front brake and rocking the bike. Until someone has checked, a knock from the front end is safety-critical: it could be a loose headset, stem or caliper. Slight headset play, once confirmed, is needs-service and a quick fix (`HEADSET-ADJUST`); a headset loose enough that the fork visibly moves stays safety-critical. A genuine fork knock usually means worn bushings, a service. A knock from the rear can be worn frame pivots (`PIVOT-SERVICE`) or shock bushings.
r1.heading: Knocking from the front

r1.content: A creak when pulling on the bar or braking hard can come from the headset, the stem or bar clamps, or a loose front thru-axle. Check for play by holding the front brake and rocking the bike. Slight play is needs-service, usually an adjustment (`HEADSET-ADJUST`); worn bearings need a service (`HEADSET-SERVICE`). Bars or a fork that visibly move are safety-critical.
r1.heading: Creak from the front of the bike

r1.content: Gears that change on their own over bumps usually come from cable housing that's too short or poorly routed, a loose shifter clamp, or a frame that flexes the housing. On full-suspension bikes, housing pulled by suspension movement can cause it. It's usually an adjustment or a cable job, not new parts.
r1.heading: Ghost shifting

r1.content: On hydraulic brakes, a lever that feels soft, or comes back further each pull, usually means air in the system, which needs a bleed (`BRAKE-BLEED`). A lever that pulls to the bar is safety-critical if the bike no longer stops properly. If it still stops, it needs service (usually a bleed); if the customer doesn't know, ask whether it still stops before deciding. Very worn pads can also make the lever travel further. On mechanical brakes, a soft lever usually means cable stretch or worn housing (`BRAKE-CABLE`).
r1.heading: Soft or spongy lever

r1.content: Before blaming the fork or shock, check the setup for the rider's weight: air pressure (or spring), sag, rebound and compression settings. A lot of "broken suspension" is a bike set up for someone else, or never set up at all. Setting it up is `SUSPENSION-SETUP`, an adjustment.
